lesson.title: Necessity, Advice & Certainty
lesson.subtitle: Necessity, advice, certainty, and purpose
lesson.description: Give advice, state obligations, express certainty or reality, and explain who or what an action is for.

learning_objectives: Express obligation and advice: 必须, 得 (děi), 该, 应该, 需要, 不用, and 最好.
Express certainty, frequency, and reality: 一定, 当然, 其实, 一般, 几乎, 总, and 可.
Express purpose and beneficiaries with 为 and 为了.

metadata.audience: HSK 3.0 Level 3 learners with Level 1-2 foundations

overview.topic_description: Modal verbs, advisory adverbs, and purpose coverbs for clear everyday reasoning.
overview.focus: Note 得 read děi ("must / have to"), 不用 ("no need to"), and 为了 ("in order to").

grammar_points.title: Using 不用 (búyòng)
grammar_points.explanation: 不用 (búyòng) means “need not; no need to” (adverb).

questions.prompt: What two weekend or daily habits does the passage recommend for staying healthy?
questions.answer: Resting early each day and going out for walks on weekends when free.
questions.explanation: The second paragraph says 每天最好早点儿休息，周末有空时多出去走走.

questions.prompt: Write two sentences using 为了 and 最好 or 必须.
questions.answer: 为了准时到机场，我们明天早上必须六点起床，最好提前叫车。
questions.explanation: Use 为了 for purpose and 必须/最好 for necessity/advice.

questions.prompt: Which expression means "no need to / don’t have to"?
questions.explanation: 不用 means no need to.

questions.prompt: Which word introduces a goal ("in order to")?
questions.explanation: 为了 means in order to.
其实 means actually or in fact.

dialogue.title: Preparing for a Trip Together
dialogue.context_en: Two friends discuss what they must prepare and what they don’t need to bring.

turns.speaker: A
turns.hanzi: 明天八点出发，咱们今天必须把行李收拾好，还得早点儿睡。
turns.pinyin: Míngtiān bā diǎn chūfā, zánmen jīntiān bìxū bǎ xíngli shōushi hǎo, hái děi zǎodiǎnr shuì.
turns.english: We leave at eight tomorrow, so today we must pack our luggage and also have to sleep early.

turns.speaker: B
turns.hanzi: 当然！不过我觉得不用带太多衣服，最好只带轻便的。
turns.pinyin: Dāngrán! Búguò wǒ juéde búyòng dài tài duō yīfu, zuìhǎo zhǐ dài qīngbiàn de.
turns.english: Of course! Though I think we don’t need to bring too many clothes—it’s best to only bring light ones.

turns.speaker: A
turns.hanzi: 其实那边的宾馆一般都有洗衣机，我们需要带的也就是牙刷和护照。
turns.pinyin: Qíshí nàbiān de bīnguǎn yìbān dōu yǒu xǐyījī, wǒmen xūyào dài de yě jiùshì yáshuā hé hùzhào.
turns.english: Actually hotels there generally have washing machines, so what we need to bring is really just toothbrushes and passports.

turns.speaker: B
turns.hanzi: 为了明天不迟到，咱们应该定两个闹钟，这样一定没问题！
turns.pinyin: Wèile míngtiān bù chídào, zánmen yīnggāi dìng liǎng ge nàozhōng, zhèyàng yídìng méi wèntí!
turns.english: In order not to be late tomorrow, we should set two alarms—that way there will definitely be no problem!

patterns.title: Stating purpose with 为了
patterns.explanation_en: Place 为了 (wèile) + goal/purpose at the start of a sentence before the action.

examples.hanzi: 为了提高汉语水平，她每天坚持读课文。
examples.pinyin: Wèile tígāo Hànyǔ shuǐpíng, tā měitiān jiānchí dú kèwén.
examples.english: In order to improve her Chinese level, she reads the lesson text every day.

examples.hanzi: 为了身体健康，我们应该多锻炼。
examples.pinyin: Wèile shēntǐ jiànkāng, wǒmen yīnggāi duō duànliàn.
examples.english: For physical health, we should exercise more.

patterns.title: Giving strong advice with 最好
patterns.explanation_en: Place 最好 (zuìhǎo, "had better") before the verb phrase to give helpful advice.

examples.hanzi: 外面风很大，你最好穿件大衣。
examples.pinyin: Wàimiàn fēng hěn dà, nǐ zuìhǎo chuān jiàn dàyī.
examples.english: It’s very windy outside—you’d better put on a coat.

examples.hanzi: 发烧的时候最好去医院检查一下。
examples.pinyin: Fāshāo de shíhou zuìhǎo qù yīyuàn jiǎnchá yíxià.
examples.english: When you have a fever, you’d better go to the hospital for a checkup.

guided_building.instruction_en: Express obligation, lack of need, and general habits.

model.hanzi: 这件事你不用担心，我一定帮你办好。
model.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì nǐ búyòng dānxīn, wǒ yídìng bāng nǐ bàn hǎo.
model.english: You don’t need to worry about this—I’ll definitely get it done for you.

substitutions.cue_en: Say it’s already 11 p.m. and we ought to sleep.

model_answer.hanzi: 已经十一点了，咱们该睡觉了。
model_answer.pinyin: Yǐjīng shíyī diǎn le, zánmen gāi shuìjiào le.
model_answer.english: It’s already eleven o’clock; we ought to go to sleep.

substitutions.cue_en: Say he almost never drinks coffee at night.

model_answer.hanzi: 他晚上几乎从不喝咖啡。
model_answer.pinyin: Tā wǎnshang jīhū cóngbù hē kāfēi.
model_answer.english: He almost never drinks coffee at night.

substitutions.cue_en: Say this gift was bought for Mom.

model_answer.hanzi: 这件礼物是为妈妈买的。
model_answer.pinyin: Zhè jiàn lǐwù shì wèi māma mǎi de.
model_answer.english: This gift was bought for Mom.

paragraphs.hanzi: 工作再忙，我们也必须照顾好自己的身体。其实，保持健康一般不需要太复杂的办法。
paragraphs.pinyin: Gōngzuò zài máng, wǒmen yě bìxū zhàogù hǎo zìjǐ de shēntǐ. Qíshí, bǎochí jiànkāng yìbān bù xūyào tài fùzá de bànfǎ.
paragraphs.english: No matter how busy work is, we must take good care of our own health. Actually, staying healthy generally doesn’t require overly complicated methods.

paragraphs.hanzi: 每天最好早点儿休息，周末有空时多出去走走。为了让自己更有精神，平时也该多喝水，少吃太甜的东西。
paragraphs.pinyin: Měitiān zuìhǎo zǎodiǎnr xiūxi, zhōumò yǒukòng shí duō chūqù zǒuzou. Wèile ràng zìjǐ gèng yǒu jīngshen, píngshí yě gāi duō hē shuǐ, shǎo chī tài tián de dōngxi.
paragraphs.english: Every day it’s best to rest a bit early, and on weekends go out for walks when free. In order to have more energy, you should normally drink more water and eat fewer overly sweet things.

questions.prompt_en: What does staying healthy generally NOT require according to the passage?
What should you do to have more energy?
questions.answer_en: Drink more water and eat fewer overly sweet things.

speaking_tasks.scenario_en: Give advice to a friend who is tired using 最好, 应该, or 不用.

model_answer.hanzi: 你今天太累了，晚上不用继续工作了，最好早点儿睡觉。
model_answer.pinyin: Nǐ jīntiān tài lèi le, wǎnshang búyòng jìxù gōngzuò le, zuìhǎo zǎodiǎnr shuìjiào.
model_answer.english: You’re too tired today—you don’t need to keep working tonight; you’d better go to sleep early.

speaking_tasks.scenario_en: Explain a goal of yours using 为了.

model_answer.hanzi: 为了学好中文，我每天坚持听录音和写汉字。
model_answer.pinyin: Wèile xuéhǎo Zhōngwén, wǒ měitiān jiānchí tīng lùyīn hé xiě Hànzì.
model_answer.english: In order to learn Chinese well, I stick to listening to recordings and writing characters every day.

teaching_plan.common_pitfall: The negative of 必须 / 得 ("must") is 不用 ("need not / don’t have to"), NOT *不得 (*bù děi) or *不必须.
teaching_plan.pronunciation_focus: 一定 (yídìng) changes 一 to rising yí before fourth-tone dìng; 得 meaning "have to" is read děi (third tone).

can_do: Express obligation and advice with 必须, 得, 应该, and 最好.
Use 不用 for "no need to".
State purpose and beneficiaries with 为了 and 为.
